title: Evaluations detect equivalences in localized strict model diagrams
statement:
Use quasicategories, nerves, coherent functor categories and functor equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Fix a universe $\mathcal U$. Let $\mathcal M$ be an ordinary category with $\mathcal U$-small Hom sets and all $\mathcal U$-small limits and colimits, equipped with classes $C,F,W$. Assume that $W$ is retract closed and satisfies two-out-of-three, and that $(C,F\cap W)$ and $(C\cap W,F)$ are weak factorization systems with functorial factorizations. Here a weak factorization system consists of a factorization of every arrow into the two classes, each class being characterized by diagonal lifting against the other. Let $0$ be initial and let $\mathcal M_c$ be the full subcategory on objects $X$ with $0\to X\in C$. For a $\mathcal U$-small ordinary category $I$, let $W_I$ consist of natural transformations in $\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal M_c)$ whose components lie in $W$. In sufficiently large universes put
$$\mathcal B=N(\mathcal M_c)[W^{-1}]_\infty,\qquad \mathcal A_I=N(\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal M_c))[W_I^{-1}]_\infty.$$
Each localization is characterized by restriction giving, into every quasicategory, an equivalence on the entire functor quasicategory with the full subcategory of functors inverting the indicated arrows. Evaluation followed by localization induces $\operatorname{ev}_i^L:\mathcal A_I\to\mathcal B$ for $i\in I$. For every arrow $a$ of $\mathcal A_I$, if $\operatorname{ev}_i^L(a)$ is an equivalence for every $i\in I$, then $a$ is an equivalence. Equivalently, the induced evaluation comparison $\mathcal A_I\to\operatorname{Fun}(N(I),\mathcal B)$ is conservative, meaning that it reflects equivalences. No model structure on $\mathcal M^I$, simplicial enrichment, combinatoriality or properness is assumed. The empty category $I$ is allowed.
